title: Chief Financial Officer Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert a chief financial officer salary from hourly to annual using 38-hour weeks, plus tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates based on Fair Work and ATO data.
salarySummary: For a chief financial officer, annual pay is hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks, with super paid on top and tax applied progressively.

faqs.q: How is a chief financial officer salary calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by 38 hours per week (the standard full-time week) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $100 per hour gives $100 × 38 × 52 = $197,600 gross per year. Superannuation of 12% is then paid on top of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and a chief financial officer salary?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. A chief financial officer salary is typically well above this, often exceeding the ABS average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). CFO roles are usually covered by an award or enterprise agreement, not the minimum wage.

faqs.q: How does superannuation affect a chief financial officer's total remuneration?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of the base salary. For a CFO earning $200,000 per year, that adds $24,000 in super, but only up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. The total remuneration package (base plus super) is a common way to compare offers. Super is not included in the hourly-to-annual conversion but is an important part of the overall package.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Chief Financial Officer Salary Calculation

When you see a **chief financial officer salary** quoted as an hourly rate, converting it to an annual figure helps you compare offers or benchmark against market data. The standard formula used on this site is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a full-time week of 38 ordinary hours, which is the basis for the National Minimum Wage and most awards under the Fair Work system. For example, an hourly rate of $120 per hour gives:

$120 × 38 × 52 = $237,120 per year before tax and super.

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your pay.

### How CFO Pay Compares to Average Earnings

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. A **chief financial officer salary** is typically well above this average, often placing CFOs in the top income brackets. The ABS figure covers all full-time adults, not just executives, so CFO pay can be two to five times higher depending on the organisation and industry.

To put it in perspective, if a CFO earns $150 per hour, the annual equivalent is $150 × 38 × 52 = $296,400. That is more than $5,700 per week, compared to the average of $2,083.70. The difference highlights the seniority and responsibility of the role.

### Minimum Wage, Awards, and Casual Loading Context

While a **chief financial officer salary** is far above minimum rates, it is useful to understand the floor set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% on the same date.

Most CFOs are not covered by an award but by an enterprise agreement or individual contract. However, if a CFO were employed as a casual, a 25% casual loading would apply on top of the base rate. For example, a casual CFO on $100 per hour would receive $125 per hour including loading. Our [timesheet](/) allows you to check the box for casual loading, but note that you should enter the base hourly rate, not the loaded rate.

### Tax and Super on Your CFO Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, the next step is estimating tax and super. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) provides tax tables for fortnightly withholding, but for 2026–27 the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). For a CFO earning $237,120, the tax would be approximately $67,138 plus Medicare of $4,742, leaving about $165,240 after tax (before any offsets).

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For a CFO on $237,120, that adds $28,454 in super, but only up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. This means total remuneration (base + super) is $265,574. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details.

### Fortnightly Pay Considerations

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a CFO earning $4,560 per week ($120 per hour), the fortnightly gross is $9,120. The ATO’s fortnightly tax table helps employers withhold the correct amount. Using the 2026–27 rates, the withholding on $9,120 for someone claiming the tax-free threshold would be around $2,208 (estimate).

Remember that the formula on this site uses 52 weeks, but some years have 27 fortnightly pays. The ATO suggests additional withholding in those years to avoid a shortfall.

### Putting It All Together

A **chief financial officer salary** can be expressed in many ways: hourly, weekly, fortnightly, or annually. Using the hourly-to-annual conversion with a 38-hour week gives you a consistent baseline. Compare that to the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) data from the ABS to see where you stand. Always consider super and tax to understand your take-home pay.

For a quick estimate, use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool. Enter your base hourly rate, check the casual loading box if applicable, and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures with tax and super estimates. This is a guide only—consult a professional for your specific situation.
